componentClasses.title: Immutable upstream model repository identity, commit and advertised release label
componentClasses.boundary: A mutable friendly name, branch or model-card field locates a candidate but is not a content-complete verified model revision.

componentClasses.title: Complete weight shard inventory, index and configuration content binding
componentClasses.boundary: One shard or manifest digest is not a model package digest; absence or reordered shard index can alter the interpreted model.

componentClasses.title: Tokenizer, vocabulary, preprocessing and processor source identity
componentClasses.boundary: Changed tokenizer or preprocessor can change semantic output with weight bytes unchanged; M06 evidence must bind an actual revision.

componentClasses.title: LoRA/adapter/base-model closure and exact compatibility revisions
componentClasses.boundary: Adapter and base-model aliases cannot imply compatibility, rights, safe loading or provenance; reference and dependency graph need proof.

componentClasses.title: Config, scheduler/precision/operator declarations and any executable custom code
componentClasses.boundary: Registry data must not import/execute arbitrary code or treat an upstream package metadata digest as supply-chain trust.

alternatives.title: Upstream tags/model-card-only reference
alternatives.hypothesis: May help discovery but mutable labels and self-reported license/capability cannot satisfy immutable identity or rights.

alternatives.title: Explicit commit and all-component digest manifest
alternatives.hypothesis: Potential reproducibility for bytes only; signature, authentic issuer, license, graph closure and operational rights remain absent.

alternatives.title: Versioned signed source manifest/SBOM and bounded issuer verification
alternatives.hypothesis: Requires future qualified M18 supply and M54 authentic principal/tenant trust, M53 rights and lifecycle revocation.

alternatives.title: At-use owner-qualified local verification receipt bound to exact component graph
alternatives.hypothesis: Cannot be issued without original owner proof, current revocation, verified host M60 and hardware M07/M08 actual empirical evidence.

questions.question: What exact immutable model repository/release/revision identifier and version boundary can M14 own without reassigning M02 production identity?
Which complete weight-shard, index and config digest closure must an M14 record bind, including absent, duplicated and renamed shards?
What is the canonical tokenizer, vocabulary and processor identity and how must stale or foreign semantic processing be marked UNKNOWN?
How may adapter/LoRA/base-model revisions form an exact dependency graph, with incompatible or missing component refusal?
Which runtime-facing code/config declarations are safe metadata versus separately authorized custom-node execution under M18/M60?
How must per-component weight/tokenizer/adapter/license claims be expressed without treating a repository badge or SPDX label as legal approval?
Which signed issuer, key rotation, revocation and tenant-specific trust source can verify future model evidence without inventing M54 signoff?
What registry identity and lifetime must distinguish upstream candidate, mirrored bytes, verified local installation and runnable provider instance?
Which M02/M06 accepted production/attempt/revision identifiers must accompany a future model revision without upgrading a cached alias to master?
How are conflicting card/license/source claims, missing terms or revoked derivative permissions represented without allowing commercial output?
Which source-qualified hardware fingerprint and M08 benchmark protocol are needed before any latency/VRAM/quality card is asserted?
When may M13 warm/model-cache hint cite M14 identity without proving model availability, M09 grant, M11 process rights or M12 placement?
What provenance and versioning must cover fine-tuned derivative training input, consent and revocation when M19/M53 owners are future only?
How must namespace/tenant ownership and provenance prevent foreign-tenant references, inference and re-use across protected project boundaries?
Which signed actual owner decisions would permit any future registry endpoint, publisher or provider loading under M58/M60?
How should changed license text, revoked source or stale card invalidate downstream M15 routing, M13 prefetch and previously generated derivatives?

negativeScenarios.trigger: A stable marketing tag resolves to a different upstream commit while a stale model card still names the old revision.
Only one shard digest matches but the index or a second weight shard is missing or replaced.
Weights remain identical but a newer tokenizer/processor silently alters input semantics.
A compatible-looking adapter names an unverifiable or conflicting base model revision.
A model package metadata field suggests importing remote custom Python code during registry discovery.
A repository badge claims permissive licensing while component terms are absent or incompatible.
A signed-looking manifest has an unverified issuer or revoked signing material.
A copied local archive exists but no original-qualified manifest, storage rights or installed code proof is present.
A prior accepted M02 master points to stale M06 result revisions while a cache aliases its model identifier.
A model card reports zero latency and tiny VRAM from a nonrepresentative, unverified machine.
A cached warm-model hint is incorrectly interpreted as a live joint lease and worker dispatch permission.
A foreign tenant provides model metadata and a revoked license while a proposed public endpoint attempts to publish it.
